nina: Quick RFC follow-up: choose explicit offload tokens vs implicit page-hints. jotting tradeoffs.

paul: short: explicit = predictable restores, easier to batch; implicit = tiny API but surprises on sync paths.

reza: fragmentation is the killer. small-page restores blow up PCIe and syscall overhead. we need coalescing.

nina: proposal: hybrid allocator flag OFFLOAD_MODE={EXPLICIT,HINTED}. default EXPLICIT for model weights and kvcache. HINTED for ephemeral guest allocations.

paul: agree. runtime needs token table for explicit mode and a compaction/coalescer for hinted mode. also quotas per-tenant for host staging.

infra-bot: canary.evictions: started; id=canary-999; note=inject-small-page-frag

reza: API sketch for explicit tokens:
```
offload_token_t offload(void* ptr);
int restore_async(offload_token_t t, restore_handle_t* out);
int poll_restore(restore_handle_t h, void** out_ptr);
int restore_sync(offload_token_t t, void** out_ptr);
```
This decouples address space from lifecycle; helps compaction.

paul: telemetry we must record: avg_fragment_size histogram, coalesced_bytes_per_restore, memcpy_calls_per_restore, restore_latency p50/p95, rejected_offloads.

nina: failure modes: if host staging is full, prefer fail-fast ENOSPC; offer fallback to compression or queue with backpressure rather than silent slowdowns.

reza: implement async restore queue with per-tenant concurrency=quota and feed it a coalescer that merges adjacent pages into larger memcpy ops.

paul: action items: nina write RFC addendum; reza implement async queue; infra add telemetry and canary injection. target EOW.

nina: leaving thread open for comments; if anyone strongly prefers hinted-only, explain mitigation for memcpy cliff.
